slot.brief: Show a wavefront diagram (spherical/plane) and ask which Huygens' principle statement correctly explains wavefront propagation / secondary wavelets.

stem: The wavefronts and direction of propagation are shown. Which statement of Huygens' principle describes the propagation of the wavefront?
options: Each point on a wavefront emits secondary wavelets, whose rear envelope forms the next wavefront.
The rays are secondary sources, and the wavelets travel along the wavefront.
Only the endpoints of a wavefront emit wavelets, and their envelope forms the new wavefront.
Each point on a wavefront emits secondary wavelets, whose forward envelope after a time interval is the new wavefront.

verdicts.working: Huygens’ principle says every point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary wavelets; their forward envelope after a time interval is the new wavefront.

working:
Every point on the existing wavefront acts as a source of secondary wavelets.
After a time interval, the forward envelope of these wavelets is the new wavefront.

Independent check: Huygens’ principle says every point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary wavelets; their forward envelope after a time interval is the new wavefront.
solution: Each point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary wavelets. After a time interval, their forward envelope forms the new wavefront.

figure.description: Draw two parallel vertical line segments to represent plane wavefronts. Label the left segment AB and the right segment A'B'. Add a horizontal arrow pointing right between them, perpendicular to both segments, to indicate the direction of propagation. Do not draw secondary wavelets or label any statement as correct.

draft.working:

draft.distractor_notes:

B: incorrectly treats rays as the secondary sources.
D: incorrectly restricts secondary wavelet sources to the endpoints.
